title: Informal help-seeking among Peruvian women exposed to intimate partner violence: A cross-sectional analysis of violence characteristics in the 2023 Demographic and Health Survey
content:
by Yordanis Enriquez Canto, Giovani Díaz Gervasi, Luis Menacho Alvirio

Background

Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major public health problem in Peru, yet many women who experience it do not seek help. We examined how the characteristics of IPV and individual and sociocultural factors are associated with help-seeking among Peruvian women exposed to physical and/or sexual IPV.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 Peruvian Demographic and Health Survey (ENDES). The analytic sample comprised 5,584 women aged 15–49 years who reported lifetime physical and/or sexual violence by a current or former partner and were asked whether they had ever sought help. Guided by the help-seeking model, we fitted three nested, survey-weighted logistic regression models (individual, interpersonal, and sociocultural factors), accounting for the complex sampling design. Discrimination was assessed with the area under the ROC curve (AUC). We also examined the number of IPV types experienced (emotional, physical, sexual).

Results

Overall, 45.0% (95% CI 42.4–47.7) of women had sought help; the most frequent reasons for not doing so were thinking it was not necessary (41.2%) and shame (16.2%). In the fully adjusted model, help-seeking was more likely among women who experienced severe physical IPV (OR 1.51; 95% CI 1.15–1.98), emotional IPV (OR 1.33; 1.05–1.67), and health problems due to violence (OR 2.22; 1.75–2.81), and was slightly less likely with increasing age (OR 0.99 per year; 0.97–1.00). Sexual IPV, region, area of residence, household wealth, and sex of the household head were not associated with help-seeking. Compared with women who experienced one type of IPV, those who experienced two (OR 1.40; 1.11–1.77) or three types (OR 1.70; 1.24–2.35) were more likely to seek help. The interpersonal model discriminated moderately (AUC 0.65); adding sociocultural factors did not improve it.

Conclusions

Among Peruvian women exposed to physical and/or sexual IPV, help-seeking is concentrated among those whose violence is more severe, multiple in form, or damaging to health, while a majority of women with less visible forms of violence do not seek help. Screening in health services that does not depend on women disclosing, and community strategies that help women and their relatives recognize violence earlier, may reach women who currently remain without support. Given the cross-sectional design and lifetime measures, these associations should not be interpreted as causal.
author: Yordanis Enriquez Canto
